faq.q: What is the etymology of Abednego?
faq.a: A Babylonian name imposed on the Hebrew Azariah: עֶבֶד (ʿeved) 'servant' + the theophoric element Nego (commonly identified with the Babylonian god Nabu). It is not a Hebrew name in origin.

faq.q: Does Abednego appear in the Bible?
faq.a: Yes. The personal name occurs in the Hebrew Bible (Daniel 1:7; 3:12-30).

faq.q: Is Abednego a Biblical name?
faq.a: Yes — the personal name occurs in the Biblical text. The personal name occurs in the Hebrew Bible (Daniel 1:7; 3:12-30).

faq.q: Does Abednego occur in the Old Testament?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: Does Abednego occur in the New Testament?
faq.a: No — it is not attested in the New Testament.

faq.q: Is Abednego associated with a saint?
faq.a: No saint association is verified for the name Abednego.

faq.q: Is the meaning of Abednego verified?
faq.a: The meaning “Servant of Nego (Nabu); a Babylonian name given to Azariah” is supported by Old Testament: the Babylonian name of Azariah, one of the three men delivered from the fiery furnace (Daniel 1:7; 3). Confidence: HIGH.

faq.q: What is the numerology or lucky number of Abednego?
faq.a: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Abednego total 53, reducing to 8. Number 8 is traditionally associated with ambition, authority and material success. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What are the common spelling variants of Abednego?
faq.a: Variants and alternative forms include Abed-nego, Abdenago.

faq.q: What is the transliteration of Abednego?
faq.a: Abednego is transliterated as ʿAved-Nego.

faq.q: How many syllables does Abednego have?
faq.a: Abednego has 4 syllables.

faq.q: What are the spiritual connotations of Abednego?
faq.a: Any spiritual significance attached to Abednego is interpretive. Its documented core is the lexical meaning “Servant of Nego (Nabu); a Babylonian name given to Azariah”, and readings built on that meaning are presented as tradition rather than as religious doctrine.

faq.q: Where is the name Abednego used today?
faq.a: Abednego circulates chiefly in Biblical Aramaic, English, Greek, Latin naming communities. No verified registration statistics are published for it.
